html:
Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was the leader of the Bengali movement against rule from West Pakistan and the founding leader of Bangladesh. Bangladeshis call him Bangabandhu, friend of Bengal.

Born in 1920, he started in the Muslim League as a student in Calcutta and backed Pakistan. After 1947 he soon turned against the dominance of West Pakistan. He was jailed during the Bengali Language Movement and rose to lead the Awami League. His Six Point plan of 1966 demanded self rule for East Pakistan.

In the 1970 election, held just after the Bhola cyclone, his party won a clear majority in all of Pakistan. The military refused to hand over power. On 25 March 1971 the army launched a crackdown and arrested him. The Bangladesh Liberation War followed, and with Indian help under Indira Gandhi Bangladesh won in December 1971.

He returned in January 1972 to lead the new state through ruin. In 1975 he set up one party rule. That August army officers killed him and most of his family. His daughter Sheikh Hasina later became prime minister.
sum: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was the leader of the Bengali movement against rule from West Pakistan and the founding leader of Bangladesh. Bangladeshis call him Bangabandhu, friend of Bengal.
